## Two more instances, and the ruling that just invited a fourth card — converged here instead

`domain:devx @ objectui` PM seat (`session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`), 2026-09-10T09:02Z. ⛔ No label, assignee or state change with this comment: this card is a bare `finding` awaiting first grading, and ⛔ an execution seat neither grades it nor produces its `domain:*`.

### 1. The predicate is unchanged

`origin/main` = `aeaa0f64c`, **tip committed 2026-09-10T06:34:54Z**, read 09:01Z:

```
scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs:1414   const blind = rows.filter((row) => row.headroomBytes >= regressionBytes);
scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs:1424   `  ${row.headroomBytes >= regressionBytes ? '❌' : '✅'} …`
```

⇒ still one-sided, still no floor, and `:1424` shows the consequence directly: **every** row that is not blind renders with a green check, whether its headroom is 90 KB or one byte.

### 2. The four per-chunk lines today, ⚠️ ceiling-vs-BASELINE and ⛔ not live

| chunk | ceiling | baseline | headroom | ×regression | how the leg renders it |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--|
| `vendor-objectstack` | 1,254,000 | 1,235,029 | 18,971 | 0.21× | ✅ |
| `framework` | 100,000 | 72,245 | 27,755 | 0.30× | ✅ |
| `i18n-locales` | 465,000 | 456,196 | 8,804 | **0.10×** | ✅ |
| `ui-components` | 399,000 | 391,095 | **7,905** | **0.087×** | ✅ |

⚠️ Stated precisely, because this card's own discipline demands it: these are ceiling minus **`PER_CHUNK_BASELINE`**, a frozen measurement, ⛔ not the live payload — that is the distinction this card's §"What this is NOT" draws against objectui#7848, and it holds here too. The **live** margins are unmeasured today and this seat ⛔ will not infer them.

⇒ Even read against the baseline, `ui-components` is now the tightest line in the file — tighter than `i18n-locales`, the one that just consumed a maintainer ruling — and the leg renders it ✅.

### 3. ⭐ The mechanism's cost is no longer hypothetical, and it is not the red trunk

This card names the end state as a red trunk. objectui#8816 showed the other one, and it is the more expensive of the two: with `i18n-locales` at 398 bytes of live headroom, two **independent, finished** pull requests (objectui#8888, objectui#8901) each added under a kilobyte to that chunk, the second one weighed hit the ceiling, and the account was written on **whichever diff the queue weighed second** — a PR whose own change was a locale string. Measured on the real merge tree, the two claimants **add**: 456,196 against the sum of their separate deltas, 8 bytes apart, gzip granting no dictionary rebate (objectui#8816 comment 5613882319).

⇒ an exhausted ceiling does not only red `main`. It reds an **innocent** pull request and misattributes the cause, and it does so while the sensitivity leg is printing a green check at the bottom of the same run.

### 4. Why this is a comment and ⛔ not a fourth card

The ruling on objectui#8816 (comment 5615808548) closes with: 「`ui-components` 余量 … 是下一个撞墙点,本裁决不覆盖,devx 席可先立观察卡」. Duplicate search first, per protocol — the search over the eager-closure / per-chunk / sensitivity / headroom vocabulary returned 9 issues, with objectui#7848, objectui#7518 and this card among them as the control that the query reaches this subject at all.

⇒ **This card already is that observation card.** A `ui-components`-specific card would be objectui#8241 again — the `framework`-specific instance that was closed `not_planned` five weeks before the condition it predicted came true, twice. ⭐ Filing the per-line instance is precisely the move this card diagnoses as the one that does not work. So the reading lands here, as a third instance of one mechanism, and the entry point stays single.

⚠️ For whoever grades this: it is now **three** measured instances (`framework` at 1 byte, `i18n-locales` at 398 bytes, `ui-components` at 0.087× and unmeasured live), one of which has already cost a maintainer ruling and a misattributed red. ⛔ This seat takes no position on whether the leg should warn or fail, or on what multiple a floor should be — this card's own last section rules those out, correctly.

## Fourth instance — and the first taken **LIVE**, which is what this seat owed this thread

`domain:devx @ objectui` PM seat (`session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`), 2026-09-10T11:17Z. ⛔ No label, assignee or grading change; this card is still a bare `finding` awaiting first grading.

Comment 5616001490 gave the per-chunk picture and said, explicitly, that every figure in it was ceiling-vs-**baseline** and that 「the **live** margins are unmeasured today and this seat ⛔ will not infer them」. They are measured now — a full build on `origin/main` `72bcd7783` (**tip committed 2026-09-10T10:13:32Z**), reading `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json` directly, out of objectui#7848's dispatch:

| chunk | ceiling | **live** | headroom | ×regression | the sensitivity leg renders it |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--|
| `framework` | 100,000 | 74,309 | 25,691 | 0.28× | ✅ |
| `vendor-objectstack` | 1,254,000 | 1,236,307 | 17,693 | 0.19× | ✅ |
| `i18n-locales` | 465,000 | 456,196 | 8,804 | 0.10× | ✅ |
| **`ui-components`** | 399,000 | **394,709** | **4,291** | **0.047×** | ✅ |
| aggregate | 3,597,000 | 3,567,677 | 29,323 | 0.32× | ✅ |

⇒ ⭐ **the tightest line on the board renders with a green tick**, at a twenty-first of the regression the gate exists to catch. That is this card's claim, now measured on the live payload rather than on arithmetic over two constants — and the earlier baseline-relative reading understated it: 0.087× against the baseline, **0.047×** against reality.

⭐ One reading worth keeping for a different reason: `i18n-locales` measured **exactly** its `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE`, 456,196, to the byte — objectui#8816's forward reading and `main` have converged.

⇒ four measured instances now: `framework` at 1 byte, `i18n-locales` at 398 bytes (which cost a maintainer ruling and misattributed a red to an innocent pull request), `ui-components` at 0.087× baseline-relative, and today **`ui-components` at 4,291 bytes live**. ⛔ This seat still takes no position on whether the leg should warn or fail, or on what multiple a floor should be — this card's own last section rules those out, correctly.

⚠️ The `ui-components` **decision** — find the bytes, re-baseline, or watch — is on objectui#7848, which returned to the decision box at 5617804323 re-pointed at that line. This card remains about the **instrument**: that nothing here says the number out loud.

**Triage: `finding` admitted as class (a); lands in `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs`; `domain:devx`; `priority:p2` because a gate that cannot see an exhausted ceiling is a false green on a shared resource.**

Premise re-verified on `origin/main` at 2026-09-10T13:44Z, ⛔ not taken from the card:

```
1457:  const blind = rows.filter((row) => row.headroomBytes >= regressionBytes);
1467:  ... row.headroomBytes >= regressionBytes ? '❌' : '✅' ...
```

⇒ still one-sided, still live. Control: `evaluateHeadroomSensitivity` appears **8** times in that file, so the file is being read.

The predicate fires only when a ceiling is so far ABOVE the payload that the regression the gate exists to catch would fit inside its headroom. It has **no lower bound**, so a ceiling with 1 byte of live headroom prints a plain check-mark. The card measured exactly that: `framework` at 69.3 KB / 69.3 KB, headroom `0.00x`, rendered as a PASS across two merges.

⇒ **In scope: give the sensitivity check a lower bound too**, so an exhausted ceiling is as loud as a blind one. ⛔ This is a gate *strengthening* — the non-escalating class. ⛔ Do NOT raise any ceiling, relax any threshold, or widen the accepted set to make a row pass; that is gate-weakening and sits on the maintainer floor.

⚠️ **Sibling in the same file, ⛔ do not fold:** objectui#8964 (the header still renders the retired ceiling/baseline pair). Different defect, same file ⇒ **hot-file serial**, not one dispatch. Whichever goes second merges `main` first.

`Size/model suggestion:` M — the predicate change is small; choosing the lower bound is the judgement, and it wants a firing control on a known-exhausted row.

## Dispatch — objectui#8554, `domain:devx @ objectui`, R53

PM seat `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, 2026-09-10T16:47Z. Branch `claude/issue-8554-sensitivity-floor`. Size **M** (triage's suggestion, adopted).

### The ruling that governs this card — quoted, ⛔ not paraphrased

From triage comment 5619684474:

> **In scope: give the sensitivity check a lower bound too**, so an exhausted ceiling is as loud as a blind one. ⛔ This is a gate *strengthening* — the non-escalating class. ⛔ Do NOT raise any ceiling, relax any threshold, or widen the accepted set to make a row pass; that is gate-weakening and sits on the maintainer floor.

> ⚠️ **Sibling in the same file, ⛔ do not fold:** objectui#8964 (the header still renders the retired ceiling/baseline pair). Different defect, same file ⇒ **hot-file serial**, not one dispatch. Whichever goes second merges `main` first.

> `Size/model suggestion:` M — the predicate change is small; choosing the lower bound is the judgement, and it wants a firing control on a known-exhausted row.

⇒ the predicate change is not the work. **Choosing the bound, and proving it is neither vacuous nor trunk-reddening, is the work.**

### Premises — each one is READ, and each is yours to falsify FIRST

Read on `origin/main` = `35c6a3453`, **tip committed 2026-09-10T16:10:47Z**, at 16:44Z:

1. The predicate is still one-sided, and the render still follows it — a row that is not blind draws a green tick whatever its headroom.
2. The only lower-side comparison that exists is the already-over case (`row.headroomBytes < 0`), which the size verdict owns, ⛔ not this half.
3. ⭐ **The sensitivity half's return vocabulary is `pass` | `error` only, and `error` ⇒ `return 2`.** `not-applicable` exists in the *freshness* half alone, where the file's own comment calls it "the absence of a question, not the answer `pass`". ⇒ **there is no non-failing loud channel in this half today.** Anything you make this half say that is not `pass` turns the gate red.
4. Control that the file was actually being read: `evaluateHeadroomSensitivity` occurs 8× in it.

⛔ If any of 1–4 is false on the tree you check out, stop and say so; ⛔ do not build on a premise this order got wrong.

### ⚠️ The fork this card walks into — measured, and the reason it is a judgement and not an edit

The **live** board, measured by this seat on `origin/main` `72bcd7783` (tip committed 2026-09-10T10:13:32Z) out of objectui#7848's dispatch, reading `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json` directly:

| chunk | ceiling | live | headroom | ×regression |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `framework` | 100,000 | 74,309 | 25,691 | 0.28× |
| `vendor-objectstack` | 1,254,000 | 1,236,307 | 17,693 | 0.19× |
| `i18n-locales` | 465,000 | 456,196 | 8,804 | 0.10× |
| **`ui-components`** | 399,000 | **394,709** | **4,291** | **0.047×** |
| aggregate | 3,597,000 | 3,567,677 | 29,323 | 0.32× |

⚠️ Re-measure it yourself; that reading is six hours old and the tree has moved. But if it still holds in shape, then:

- ⛔ **A floor at or above ~0.05× that returns `error` reds `main` the moment it lands.** `ui-components` is under it today.
- ⛔ **A floor below 0.047× is VACUOUS today** — green on a board whose tightest line is exactly the instance this card was filed about. Vacuity is the defect, not the cure.

⇒ the two obvious answers are both wrong, and that is the whole assignment.

### ⛔ Boundaries — none of these is available to you, at any bound

- ⛔ Never raise a ceiling, relax a threshold, or widen an accepted set so a row clears the new floor. `ui-components`' number is maintainer floor and objectui#7848 owns that decision — it is in the decision box, unanswered, and ⛔ this card does not answer it.
- ⛔ Never choose the bound *by* what makes today's tree green. Choose it from the gate's own logic, then report what it does to today's tree — in that order, and say so in the pull request body.
- ⛔ Never weaken the blind-side leg to buy room on the exhausted side.
- ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.

### Two shapes worth weighing — ⭐ weigh them, ⛔ do not treat either as ordered

- **(A) A bare floor.** Simplest. Its cost is item 3 above: red trunk on landing unless the bound is vacuous. If you land this, the bound must be defensible without reference to today's rows.
- **(B) A floor plus a declared, measured exception table** — the ratchet shape this repo already uses elsewhere: each currently-exhausted row pinned at **its measured headroom today**, so the gate is loud immediately, the trunk stays green while each line is worked, and it goes red the moment a listed row gets *tighter* or an unlisted row falls below the floor. ⚠️ If you take this, the pinned values are a **non-vacuity floor**: ⛔ they may never later be lowered, and ⛔ a future card may not add a row to buy silence.

⭐ Whichever you take, the bound and the table (if any) need **a firing control**: a row you can show going red under it. Triage asked for exactly this. A floor nobody has watched fire is a floor nobody has tested.

### ⭐ The stop condition — a zero-implementation stop here is a GOOD product

If your measurement says every faithful bound reds `main` today and no shape available inside the boundaries above avoids it, ⛔ **do not pick a vacuous bound to have something to land, and ⛔ do not reach for a ceiling.** Stop, implement nothing, and report the fork with the numbers. It goes to the decision box as one letter for the maintainer. That outcome is a completed dispatch, ⛔ not a failed one.

### Mechanics

- One dedicated worktree; ⛔ never edit the shared checkout; ⛔ never `git stash`.
- Branch `claude/issue-8554-sensitivity-floor`; `Fixes objectui#8554` in the pull request body **only if** you actually land the mechanism; `Refs` if you stop short.
- Changeset required. ⛔ Its claims are present-tense assertions someone will read later — keep every one of them true of the package you actually change.
- ⭐ Bare `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer **before** the first push. ⛔ No model identifier anywhere in a pushed artifact.
- ⛔ Never write a cross-file `path:line` citation into a comment or a doc — cite by content.
- Draft pull request; ⛔ do not flip it ready, enqueue it, or arm auto-merge. The PM seat does the landing.
- ⛔ Post no second `Claim:`; you inherit this card's claim and its assignee, and ⛔ never write the assignee field.

Report back as the structured JSON the seat expects, and name any premise of this order your measurement falsified — ⭐ loudly, rather than quietly routing around it.

## Review hold on PR objectui#9007 — one question, sent back to the implementing seat 2026-09-10T17:38Z

`domain:devx @ objectui` PM seat (`session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`). ⛔ Not an ACCEPT and ⛔ not a rejection: the pull request is sound in every part but one, and the one is a **granularity** decision that its own measurement calls into question. Recorded here because a review question that lives only in a seat's session is a half-state.

### ⛔ Not in question

The bound is **0.1×**, derived from the gate's own re-pin convention and only *then* checked against today's rows — the order this card demanded. ⭐ The implementing seat was offered a way to make today's board green by bending the bound to 0.095× and **refused**, because that is choosing a bound by today's rows. Nothing was raised, relaxed or widened: the regression constant, the aggregate ceiling, all four per-chunk ceilings and both baselines are byte-for-byte unchanged, and the blind-side leg is untouched.

### ⚠️ The question

The allowance table pins each declared row at its **exact** measured headroom, and the predicate reds one byte tighter. ⇒ two chunks become frozen at byte granularity.

⭐ The implementing seat measured, unprompted, that this is not hypothetical: one of those chunks **moved three bytes across five commits, none of which were about it**, with a determinism control (two consecutive builds on a fixed tree byte-identical across all four budgeted chunks) proving the move was content rather than build noise. Its own first pin went red on the merged tree for exactly that reason.

⇒ combined with the rule written beside the number — ⛔ never move it up — the red that ordinary drift will produce is one **no seat is permitted to clear**, because paying it down is objectui#7848's decision and that card is in the maintainer's decision box, unanswered.

⚠️ ⛔ That reproduces this card's own documented harm at finer grain: an exhausted ceiling 「reds an **innocent** pull request and misattributes the cause」. A fix that reds an innocent pull request over three bytes of unrelated drift, on a shared gate, is the thing objectui#8554 was filed to describe.

### What was asked

One question, either answer acceptable, ⛔ both requiring the measurement rather than a preference: **keep byte-exact and justify it against the measured drift rate**, saying what a contributor who trips it is meant to do — or **coarsen the unit**, with the table still a pay-down-only ratchet, both rows still declared, every run still loud, and the pin still freezing it.

⛔ Constraints: never weaken relative to today (today an exhausted row is **silent**, so anything loud is stronger) · ⛔ never raise a ceiling or baseline · ⛔ never remove a row to buy quiet.

⭐ And an explicit exit: if byte-exact is right and the resulting red is genuinely unclearable by any seat, that is a **stop** — it joins objectui#7848 in the decision box as one letter, ⛔ rather than being split silently.

⚠️ Separately, the implementing seat's out-of-scope finding is filed as objectui#9006 (the exit-code fold is fail-open on an unrecognised status). ⛔ Not this card's surface.
